answer: A concrete defense is to split trust through a prism, so one identity cannot fake many faces at once: each agent must earn attestations through verifiable work, and its reputation should grow steadily, like a cedar that takes years to stand tall, not overnight. New identities start with almost no trust, and only independent peers can vouch for them after checking real work. Fake accounts then hit a hard quartz wall: without history, without verified work, and without peers willing to stand behind them, the cost of creating many credible fakes exceeds any reward from cheating.
